"Keep going and driving until we have a working rust implementation." 25. Harness amendment A7 (stage 2, bench-verified 2026-11-10, reviewer to confirm), record df7d421e, two findings. (a) fth 0.1.2 judges a test's plan `metrics` by text alone at window close (fth/checks.py judge(): PredSpec(name) without the helper binding), so every helper-bound metric raised `PlanError: unparsable predicate` (L0-1, L2-4, L4-1, L7-1 FAIL); moving them to `all_of` is refused too (a test-owned plan must not mix in plan-owned checks: it would lose the stimulus pin and the replay auditor). tests.title: SET_LIMIT queue-full -> BUSY (overflow hook)
tests.purpose: Bursts twelve SET_LIMIT commands into the queued Rust monitor within one dispatch to prove the component queue fills at ten and the Rust overflow hook answers BUSY for the rest, with no assert, no silent drop and a later SET_LIMIT accepted.
tests.covers_note: the burst is issued by the harness tester (rustTester.BURST_CMD_U32) through cmdDisp's sequencer port, so the dispatcher itself logs OpCodeDispatched/Completed/OpCodeError(BUSY) for every command
tests.setup: L6-1 passed; limit at 4294967295; no rustCounter command in the preceding 2 s and >= 1 s since any previous burst (rustCounter.countOut shares RustMonitor's 10-deep queue: a BUMP/RESET in the preceding second makes copy 10 BUSY too; lens measured 8/8 bursts -> exactly 2 BUSY under this precondition).
tests.evidence: A22: to be recorded from the re-cycle clean record and the burst_too_small vector

rationale.text: queue depth Default.QUEUE_SIZE = 10 (instances.fpp:25), drained once per 1 Hz run: twelve commands emitted inside one dispatch land in one period, ten queue, two are answered BUSY by the overflow hook (RustMonitor.rs SET_LIMIT_overflow_hook) and surface as cmdDisp.OpCodeError(error=BUSY) (CommandDispatcherImpl.cpp:84-89). Both handlers run on cmdDisp's thread inside one dispatch, so the burst never straddles a run(); the only other queue user is rustCounter.countOut (async drop), excluded by the setup precondition (A22)
every queued command is delivered on the next run (REQ-RustMonitor-005); ten accepted limits = ten LimitSet(7)
after the burst the queue is empty again: a later SET_LIMIT completes normally (no stuck BUSY state)
the 12-command burst fits cmdDisp's 20-deep queue (CdhCoreConfig.fpp:9); EventsDropped == 0: the burst's 17 events fit the 40-deep events queue

tests.title: Final state
tests.purpose: Saves THRESHOLD 42 into the parameter file, downlinks the file into the record and resets the counter to leave the deployment in an independently verifiable state.
tests.covers_note: final-state evidence (THRESHOLD persistence in PrmDb.dat) is owned by the autocoded parameter base + Svc.PrmDb, not traced to a component row (decision log 11)
procedure: action: the recorder's GDS stores downlinked files under {logs}/files (bench gds --file-storage-directory), i.e. record/raw/files/fprime-downlink/PrmDb.dat; the prmdb_record_equals check parses it (CRC32, 0xA5 delimiter, U32 record size, FwPrmIdType id, value; Svc/PrmDb/docs/sdd.md §3.2)

rationale.text: THRESHOLD is the only parameter in the deployment, so the saved file holds exactly one record

stimulus-declared helper check `counter_advances(channel="relay.Relayed", by=1)` (A7: fth 0.1.2 judges plan `metrics` by text alone, so a helper-bound check is declared by the test with check(text, helper) and bound through this plan's helpers module); the reset count 0 travels Rust→C++→Rust one more time

stimulus-declared helper check `prmdb_record_equals(path="files/fprime-downlink/PrmDb.dat", id=268525568, value=42)` (A7: fth 0.1.2 judges plan `metrics` by text alone, so a helper-bound check is declared by the test with check(text, helper) and bound through this plan's helpers module)

stimulus-declared check (A13): under skip_reset no count travels the port chain and LastCount has no sample in the window; fth 0.1.2 promotes a sample-less stimulus check to FAIL on a complete window but leaves a plan metric UNVERIFIED and out of `failed`, so the predicate is declared by the test to keep the planted fault's fails set byte-exact

stimulus-declared check (A14): Svc.FileDownlink queues SendFile and answers the command OK before opening the file; a missing PrmDb.dat surfaces as the asynchronous WARNING_HI FileOpenError (`Could not open file PrmDb.dat`), never as cmdDisp.OpCodeError. This is the predicate the threshold_not_saved fault fails together with the absent-file helper check.

tests.evidence: PrmFileSaveComplete(1), FileSent, ResetIssued; Counter 0; LastCount 0; Relayed +1; record/raw/files/PrmDb.dat holds THRESHOLD (0x10016000) = 42.
